verdict.summary: You can create a Slack app and connect your own workspace in minutes. Turning on distribution lets other workspaces install it with no review. Slack's policy, though, says commercially distributed apps must go through the Slack Marketplace. That needs 10+ active workspaces first, and review can take up to 10 weeks. Broad scopes such as search:read.* and *:history also trigger enhanced review.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min for a working app; 1-3 days to prepare Marketplace assets (landing page, privacy policy, demo video, scope justifications)
verdict.approval_wait: none for direct installs on other workspaces; Marketplace listing takes up to 10 business days for preliminary review plus up to 10 weeks for functional review

gates.name: Development workspace
gates.unlocks: The app can be installed and authorized on the one workspace you picked when you created it.
limits: Works only on the workspace that created the app. Other workspaces get invalid_team_for_non_distributed_app
The authorization code expires after 10 minutes
Tokens don't expire unless you turn on token rotation (then access tokens last 12 hours)

gates.name: Distributed (unlisted) app
gates.unlocks: Any workspace you send the install link to can install the app through OAuth.
limits: Needs an OAuth 2.0 flow and HTTPS for redirect, interaction, options-load and Events API URLs
There is no test-user allowlist. Anyone with the link can install
Enterprise orgs reject scopes that aren't org-compatible (scope_not_allowed_on_enterprise)
Slack's policy requires commercially distributed apps to be submitted to the Marketplace
gates.time_to_reach: Minutes after you turn on distribution and set HTTPS URLs

gates.name: Slack Marketplace listing
gates.unlocks: A public listing in the Slack Marketplace, which Slack's policy requires for commercial distribution.
limits: You can't submit until the app is installed on at least 10 active workspaces (used in the last 28 days)
Search:read.*, *:history, files:read and admin.* scopes get enhanced review. Admin/identity/search:read scopes are unlikely to be approved
After publishing, any scope change needs re-review or installs fail with unapproved_scope
gates.time_to_reach: Up to 10 business days for preliminary review plus up to 10 weeks for functional review (6 weeks for resubmissions of published apps), after you reach 10 active workspaces

steps.title: Sign in and create the Slack app
steps.detail: Go to api.slack.com/apps, sign in to your Slack account, and create a new app. Enter an App Name and choose the Development Workspace where you'll build and test it.
gotchas: The app works only on this workspace until you turn on distribution.

steps.title: Add the Composio redirect URL
steps.detail: In OAuth & Permissions, add a Redirect URL. Paste the exact callback URL shown in your Composio auth config.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: The URL must be HTTPS and can't contain a '#'.
The redirect_uri sent in each request must match a configured Redirect URL or be a subdirectory of one.

steps.title: Choose a narrow scope set
steps.detail: Have an agent list the bot scopes (scope) and user scopes (user_scope) your features actually use, and add them in OAuth & Permissions. Composio's default list includes search:read.* and *:history. Leave those out unless you need them, because they trigger enhanced Marketplace review.
gotchas: Optional scopes still have to be demonstrated during review.
Requesting scopes for future features gets the submission rejected.

steps.title: Decide on token rotation
steps.detail: By default tokens don't expire. If you turn on token rotation in OAuth & Permissions, access tokens expire after 12 hours and are refreshed with single-use refresh tokens. Make sure Composio's refresh handling fits before you enable it.
gotchas: You can't turn token rotation off once it's on.

steps.title: Put the Client ID and Client Secret into Composio
steps.detail: Copy the Client ID and Client Secret from the app's settings page. Paste them into a custom Slack auth config in Composio, using the same scopes. Composio uses https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize and oauth.v2.access.

steps.title: Test-connect your development workspace
steps.detail: Start a Composio connection and approve it in your development workspace. Then check that a token comes back and that a test API call works.
gotchas: The code expires after 10 minutes, so finish the flow promptly.
Other workspaces fail with invalid_team_for_non_distributed_app until you turn on distribution.

steps.title: Turn on distribution to other workspaces
steps.detail: In the app settings, turn on distribution so other workspaces can install the app through OAuth. Every redirect, interaction, options-load and Events API URL must use HTTPS.
gotchas: Slack's policy says commercially distributed apps must also be submitted to the Marketplace.
Enterprise org installs fail with scope_not_allowed_on_enterprise if your scopes aren't org-compatible.

steps.title: Grow to 10 active workspaces
steps.detail: Get the app installed and used on at least 10 workspaces. A workspace counts as active if it used the app in the last 28 days. Test install, use and uninstall end to end on a workspace other than your development workspace.
gotchas: Slack blocks Marketplace submission until you reach 10 active workspaces.

steps.title: Prepare listing assets and policies
steps.detail: Have an agent draft four things: a public landing page (not behind a login), a privacy policy covering data collection, use, retention and deletion plus a contact method, a support page, and a 1600x1000 image set. You also need a distinctive, high-quality icon that doesn't look like Slackbot or the Slack logo, and a 30-90 second video.
gotchas: The support page must commit to responding within 2 business days.
The policy forbids training LLMs on Slack data and restricts sentiment analysis.

steps.title: Write a justification for each scope
steps.detail: Write one justification per scope that ties it to a feature that exists in the submitted app. Expect extra scrutiny for search:read.*, *:history and files:read.

steps.title: Record the demo and set up reviewer access
steps.detail: Record a public YouTube demo that shows install and OAuth, setup, end-to-end use and uninstall. Give reviewers test-account access, because Slack can't access your test workspaces and needs to install the app itself.

steps.title: Submit to the Slack Marketplace
steps.detail: Submit the app for Marketplace review from the app settings. It must be fully working, publicly installable and production-ready.

steps.title: Wait for Marketplace review
steps.detail: Preliminary review takes up to 10 business days. Functional review takes up to 10 weeks for new submissions (6 weeks for resubmissions of published apps). Slack returns submissions that have bugs or aren't production-ready.
gotchas: A resubmission keeps or resets its place in the queue depending on whether a reviewer was already assigned.

requirements.item: HTTPS redirect URL with no anchor
requirements.detail: Redirect URLs must be HTTPS and contain no '#'. The redirect_uri in each request must match a configured URL or be a subdirectory of one.
OAuth redirect, interaction, options-load and Events API URLs must all support SSL.
You need at least 10 workspaces that used the app in the last 28 days before you can submit.

requirements.item: Public landing page, privacy policy and support page
requirements.detail: The landing page can't be behind a login. The privacy policy must cover data collection, use, retention and deletion and give a contact method. Support must respond within 2 business days.
A 1600x1000 image set, a 30-90 second video, and a distinctive icon that doesn't look like Slack's.
A public demo of install, OAuth, use and uninstall, plus test-account access so the reviewer can install the app.
No LLM training on Slack data, restricted sentiment analysis, no getting around paid-plan limits, and no sub-licensing API access to others.

scopes.effect: Triggers enhanced review. Slack lists search:read as unsuitable for the Marketplace without a clear use case. These scopes are in Composio's default list.
These are extensive-access *:history scopes and get enhanced Marketplace review.
Unlikely to be approved for apps outside Slack's partner program.
Standard scopes. They still need a per-scope justification tied to a working feature.
Used for Sign in with Slack (OpenID Connect) through slack.com/openid/connect/authorize. This is a separate flow from the v2 install.

blockers.cause: Distribution isn't turned on, so only the workspace that created the app can authorize it.
blockers.fix: Turn on distribution (HTTPS URLs plus OAuth) in the app settings.

blockers.cause: A published Marketplace app requested scopes that haven't been submitted or are still in review.
blockers.fix: Submit the scope change for review and wait for approval before using updated install links. Until then, request only approved scopes.

blockers.cause: The app requested scopes that aren't compatible with Enterprise orgs.
blockers.fix: Use org-compatible scopes when installing on Enterprise orgs.

blockers.symptom: Code exchange fails with an expired or invalid code
blockers.fix: Exchange the code right away and check the state parameter.

blockers.cause: The app has fewer than 10 active workspaces.
blockers.fix: Grow usage to 10+ workspaces active in the last 28 days before submitting.

blockers.cause: Bugs, a build that isn't production-ready, or unjustified or extensive scopes (e.g. Composio's default search:read.*).
blockers.fix: Narrow the scopes, justify each one, and test end to end on a workspace other than your development workspace before you resubmit.

composio.note: Start on Composio's managed Slack app for prototyping. It needs no Slack app registration. Register your own app when you need: your own branding on the consent screen, a narrower scope set, or Marketplace distribution of your product (Slack's policy requires Marketplace submission for commercial distribution). When you register your own app, paste the exact callback URL from your Composio auth config as the Redirect URL. Also trim Composio's broad default scopes (search:read.*, *:history), which trigger enhanced Marketplace review.

evidence.claim: Composio's toolkit catalog lists Slack with managed OAUTH2 available, authorization URL https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize and token URL https://slack.com/api/oauth.v2.access.
The developer portal prompts sign-in to a Slack account before an app can be created.
evidence.quote: You'll need to sign in to your Slack account to create an application.

evidence.claim: A new app is created from app settings and begins in a single development workspace.
evidence.quote: Fill out your App Name and select the Development Workspace where you'll play around and build your app.

evidence.claim: Slack uses a v2 OAuth 2.0 authorization code flow via oauth/v2/authorize and oauth.v2.access with client_id and client_secret.
The client ID is shown on the App Management page; bot scopes go in scope and user scopes in user_scope.
Redirect URLs must use HTTPS, redirect_uri must match or be a subdirectory of a configured URL, and anchors are not allowed.
Publicly distributed apps must use SSL for OAuth redirect, interaction, options load and Events API URLs.
evidence.quote: Your app must support SSL for all: OAuth redirect URLs;

evidence.claim: The OAuth authorization code expires after ten minutes, and state should be checked.
Tokens do not expire by default; with token rotation, access tokens expire after 12 hours and refresh tokens are single-use.
Token rotation cannot be turned off once enabled; for unpublished apps it is toggled in OAuth & Permissions.
Distributing to other workspaces requires OAuth 2.0 and HTTPS URLs; single-workspace apps cannot be installed elsewhere.
evidence.quote: Single-workspace apps can't be distributed to any other workspaces.

evidence.claim: Slack's lifecycle & distribution page describes the ways apps can be distributed.
Commercially distributed apps must be submitted to the Marketplace, which involves manual review.
evidence.quote: In order to commercially distribute your app, you must submit it to the Marketplace.

evidence.claim: Slack clarified on December 10, 2024 that apps for commercial distribution at scale should go through Marketplace review.
Marketplace submission requires installation on at least 10 active workspaces (active within 28 days).
evidence.quote: Your app has been installed on 10 or more active workspaces

evidence.claim: Apps with fewer than 10 active workspaces and fewer than 10 weekly active users are unsuitable for Marketplace listing.
The app must be fully functional, publicly installable, and tested end to end including uninstall on a non-development workspace.
Preliminary review takes up to 10 business days; functional review up to 10 weeks (6 weeks for resubmissions).
Submission requires a public YouTube demo of install/OAuth/use/uninstall and reviewer-installable test access.
Listing requires a public landing page, a detailed privacy policy, a support page (2 business day response), 1600x1000 images and a 30-90 second video.
Legacy, admin.*, identity.*, search:read and workflow scopes are restricted or unsuitable for the Marketplace.
Extensive-access scopes such as search:read.*, *:history, files:read and admin.* trigger enhanced review.
Scopes must be justified per scope; scopes for future features are rejected.
Scopes can be marked optional, but apps must still demonstrate all required and optional scopes.
New scopes require reinstall; Marketplace apps must submit scope changes for review or get unapproved_scope errors.
Installs of a published app requesting unapproved scopes fail with unapproved_scope.
Training LLMs on Slack data is prohibited, sentiment analysis is restricted, and circumventing paid limits is prohibited.
The policy forbids sub-licensing API access and requires a distinctive high-quality icon.
evidence.quote: You must include, with your submission, a well-designed, high quality, distinctive icon

evidence.claim: Submissions can be returned for bugs or not being production-ready; resubmission queue position depends on reviewer assignment.
Enterprise org installs requesting non-org-compatible scopes fail with scope_not_allowed_on_enterprise.
Undistributed apps can only be authorized on the creating team (invalid_team_for_non_distributed_app).
Slack's OIDC discovery advertises openid, profile and email scopes with endpoint slack.com/openid/connect/authorize.

open_questions: Composio's config mentions two callback URLs (backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add and a /api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback path). Check in your Composio auth config which one to add as the Slack Redirect URL.
Is Composio's managed Slack app itself listed in the Marketplace, and does that let you skip your own review? The sources didn't say.
The exact menu and button names for turning on distribution weren't captured. Look under the app's distribution settings.
Slack's security review requirements and the full list of Marketplace submission form fields weren't retrieved in full.
It isn't confirmed whether creating an app needs a paid Slack plan or works on a free workspace.
No rate limits specific to unreviewed or unlisted apps were found.
It's unclear whether Enterprise Grid org-wide installs need separate approval beyond scope compatibility.
It's unclear whether direct (non-Marketplace) distribution of a commercial product is enforced or only stated in policy.
